chunks: 53 – Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, Abū Muḥammad, al-Juhannī. His origin was Kufan, he resided in Basra. I saw a book in which there were lessons, preachments, and instructions about the benefits of the limbs of man and animals, and sections of kalām regarding tawḥīd, and its title was: "Questions of the student and its composition" from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī (peace be upon him). And beneath the title in the handwriting of al-Ḥusayn ibn Aḥmad ibn Shaybān al-Qazwīnī: "The student is Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, and this book is his, and these questions he asked Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) and he answered him."

key_terms.حَمَّادُ بْنُ عِيسَى: Hammād ibn ʿĪsā, a Shia narrator and scholar
key_terms.مَسَائِلُ التَّلْمِيذ: Questions of the student, referring to the title of the work

ai.seo_question: What is the content and origin of the book 'Masā'il al-Talmīdh' by Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā?
ai.summary: This biographical entry describes the scholar Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā and a book he authored titled 'Questions of the Student and its Composition'. The book contains lessons, moral exhortations, and theological discussions on tawḥīd, derived from questions he posed to Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) and the Imam's responses.
